thread:
marco: Heads up — several users hit a failure when running the sample-runner in edge with sdk@2.5.0. onboarding flow stops on import errors.

elena: Ugh, can you paste the trace?

marco: Here you go:

```
Error: Uncaught SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at internalCompileModule (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1100:18)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1151:12)
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1221:10)
    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1045:32)
    at Function.Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:898:12)
    at Module.require (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1069:19)
    at require (node:internal/modules/cjs/helpers:110:18)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/workspace/samples/edge-runner/index.js:3:1)
```

ben: That stack is classic exports/conditional-entry mismatch. Looks like our package.json only exposes conditional entries for "import"/"require" at the root but no explicit edge subpath. Edge runtime/bundlers sometimes resolve to the cjs entry and blow up because the edge sample expects ESM.

sam: Repro'd locally — sample bundler (esbuild for Cloudflare Workers) resolves `require` path if `main` exists or if the consumer environment favors CJS. Our `package.json` currently has:

```
"main": "cjs/index.js",
"module": "esm/index.js",
"exports": {
  "./": {
    "require": "./cjs/index.js",
    "import": "./esm/index.js"
  }
}
```

sam: That doesn't give a clear ESM-only subpath for edge. Quick fix is to add an explicit `./edge` export (and point to a small ESM edge entry with correct types).

elena: Proposal for exports patch (minimal):

```
"exports": {
  "./edge": {
    "import": "./esm/edge.mjs",
    "default": "./esm/index.mjs"
  },
  "./": {
    "require": "./cjs/index.js",
    "import": "./esm/index.js"
  }
}
```

elena: Also need `types` mapping for the edge subpath so TS in sample apps picks up correct typings (some users hit missing types in the edge template).

ben: Agreed. We should also avoid `main` pointing to cjs in the published artifact for new minor — that pushes consumers toward CJS when they don't use exports-aware resolvers. Might cause more edge regressions.

marco: Would publishing a patch with `./edge` + `types` fix the immediate customer reports?

sam: Yes, and add a tiny ESM wrapper `esm/edge.mjs` that imports the real entry and re-exports. That keeps runtime parity.

dev-bot: CI alert: samples-edge-integration failed on latest canary (job 432). Tests failing: "edge-runner smoke" x3.

elena: I'll open a PR with the exports + types + a sample integration test that runs the edge template via the esbuild-based runner. Will include a short note in changelog and onboarding docs.

sam: Please also add a migration note for teams who pin `main`/CJS — they may need to update.

ben: Suggest also adding a tiny check in our sample generator that ensures package.json in generated apps has no `main` set (or sets it to ESM-friendly) when target runtime is edge. Saves new users the trap.

marco: Perfect. Thanks — assign to elena. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/789 (draft).

elena: Taking it. I'll update docs on devex site and add an example `exports` snippet for edge + node.

sam: After the patch, we should run a small cohort of onboarding tests against real CF/WR environments (not just unit). I can queue that.

marco: :thumbsup:

ben: FYI — logging note: add a short log when sample detects mismatched module system to give clearer error message for users.

elena: Will do. ETA for PR end of day.
